properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 14 at 9:36AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity for the
following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage through Friday, as previous heavy rainfall continues to drain
through the basin. However, strong northeasterly winds this weekend
are forecast to lead a return to Moderate Flood Stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.8 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 14 at 6:33AM MST until October 17 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...East to southeast winds 30 to 35 mph with gusts 50-60 mph
are expected. The strongest winds may be focused immediately
downstream of the higher terrain, and along terrain gaps and
east-west oriented valleys Friday morning.

* WHERE...A portion of Southeast Arizona.

* WHEN...From 11 PM Thursday to 11 AM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Strong and gusty winds over desert areas could result in
blowing dust, briefly lowering visibility below a mile at times.
Difficult driving conditions will be present, especially for larger
vehicles traveling along roadways with strong and gusty crosswinds.
Light, unsecured objects such as trash cans and yard decorations
may be blown around. Tree limbs could be blown down and a few power
outages may result.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

FFWOUN

The National Weather Service in Norman has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Greer County in southwestern Oklahoma...
Northern Harmon County in southwestern Oklahoma...
Northern Kiowa County in southwestern Oklahoma...
Beckham County in western Oklahoma...
Custer County in western Oklahoma...
Southern Roger Mills County in western Oklahoma...
Washita County in western Oklahoma...

* Until 1030 AM CDT.

* At 721 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 7 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated and gauge reports.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Elk City, Weatherford, Clinton, Sayre, Cordell, Burns Flat, Thomas,
Erick, Sentinel, Arapaho, Mountain View, Hammon, Dill City, Canute,
Corn, Custer City, Butler, Carter, Bessie and Rocky.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
